repos.brief:
**What it does:** A prompt engineering library for GPT-Image-2 with 500+ reverse-engineered generation cases, 20+ industrial templates, and a browsable gallery at gpt-image2.canghe.ai where you can copy full prompts and filter by style or scenario.

**Why now:** The repo gained 10,191 stars this week, signaling a sharp spike in community interest around structured GPT-Image-2 prompt patterns at the moment developers are actively exploring the model.

**Build with it:** Drop one of the 20+ industrial templates directly into a call to APIMart's async GPT-Image-2 API (`$0.006/image`) to batch-generate styled assets without writing prompts from scratch.

**What it does:** Ponytail is an AI agent skill that steers your coding agent toward minimal solutions — preferring a native `<input type="date">` over installing flatpickr — cutting a measured 54% of output LOC on real FastAPI + React tasks.

**Why now:** It hit Hacker News this week (98 points, 17 comments) while gaining 9,264 GitHub stars in seven days, surfacing active builder interest in prompt-level agent constraints.

**Build with it:** Drop the ponytail skill into your Claude Code setup and run it against an existing feature branch to measure the `git diff` reduction before merging.

**What it does:** Scientific Agent Skills is a library of 163 validated research skills — spanning cancer genomics, PK/PD modelling, molecular dynamics, microbiome foundation models, and 100+ scientific databases — that plugs into any AI agent supporting the open Agent Skills standard.

**Why now:** The project gained nearly 7,000 stars this week, coinciding with a recorded onboarding webinar for K-Dense BYOK, the free local co-scientist runtime that activates all 163 skills without a managed backend.

**Build with it:** Drop the skills into a Claude Code or Cursor project via the Agent Skills config, then wire a single skill — such as the live pathogen-variant surveillance endpoint — to validate that your agent can query external scientific databases before expanding coverage.

**What it does:** Orca is a desktop/mobile AI orchestrator that runs Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, or Pi side-by-side in isolated git worktrees, letting you compare outputs and merge the winner.

**Why now:** The repo crossed 59K stars with 5,700 added this week, signaling a sharp surge in adoption likely tied to the parallel-agents workflow becoming a standard pattern among CLI-first builders.

**Build with it:** Fan a single bug-fix prompt across three parallel worktrees using Orca's built-in orchestration, then use Design Mode to click the broken UI element in the embedded Chromium window and pipe its HTML/CSS directly into the winning agent's follow-up prompt.

**What it does:** ECC is an agent harness system that adds skills, memory, security, and instinct layers on top of Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, and Cursor via MCP and npm packages.

**Why now:** The repo hit GitHub's trending-of-the-day rank this week, surfacing alongside accelerating Claude Code adoption as Anthropic's agentic tooling becomes a primary dev workflow.

**Build with it:** Install `ecc-agentshield` from npm and wire it into your Claude Code setup to add security guardrails to an existing agentic coding session.

**What it does:** OpenMontage is an open-source, agentic video production system that lets an AI coding assistant handle the full production pipeline — research, scripting, asset generation, editing, and composition — across 12 pipelines and 100+ tools.

**Why now:** The repo hit #1 on GitHub Trending this week, surfacing it to a large wave of builders actively looking for an entry point.

**Build with it:** Drop a YouTube URL into the "Paste A Video" workflow to let the agent reverse-engineer its structure and regenerate a new video in the same style using your own prompt.

**What it does:** OmniRoute is a free MIT-licensed AI gateway that routes requests across 352 providers (150+ free tiers) through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with quota-aware auto-fallback and RTK+Caveman token compression saving 15–95% of tokens.

**Why now:** The repo gained 4,865 stars this week, signaling a surge of builders actively stress-testing it — making this a live moment to catch real usage patterns and edge cases rather than synthetic ones.

**Build with it:** Point your Claude Code or Cursor `OPENAI_BASE_URL` at the OmniRoute endpoint and let the 19 routing strategies distribute quota across free tiers automatically — validating whether the ~1.51B free tokens/month headline holds for your actual workload.

**What it does:** A Claude Code-based CLI framework that scrapes job portals, scores posting fit against your profile, and runs a drafter-reviewer pipeline to produce tailored LaTeX CVs and cover letters.

**Why now:** The repo gained 4,816 stars this week, driven by the author's verified case study — 69 tailored applications, 20 first interviews, one signed offer — which is circulating as a concrete proof-of-workflow rather than a demo.

**Build with it:** Fork the repo, drop your profile into the config files, then run `/scrape` followed by `/apply <url>` on a real posting to validate the fit-scoring and LaTeX output against your own CV before touching any prompts.

**What it does:** claude-obsidian is a local-first Claude Code plugin that ingests any source file into a provenance-tracked, wikilink-connected Obsidian vault of plain Markdown—preserving source citations, claim ledgers, and confidence states across ingestion, retrieval, and maintenance workflows.

**Why now:** The repo gained 2,136 stars this week, signaling a sharp uptick in builder interest around Claude Code's plugin ecosystem at the moment Anthropic's agent tooling is maturing into a production surface.

**Build with it:** Drop a PDF or local file into the vault inbox, then wire the `capture` skill into your existing Claude Code session to get source-cited, cross-linked notes without any cloud sync or database dependency.

**What it does:** herdr is a Rust-based background server that keeps coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) running in persistent terminal panes, marking each as working, blocked, or idle so you never lose track of a stuck agent.

**Why now:** The repo gained 2,101 stars this week, signaling a surge of interest likely tied to the current wave of developers running multi-agent coding workflows who need something sturdier than a raw tmux session.

**Build with it:** Drop herdr into an existing Claude Code workflow using the documented agent skill and socket API to let one agent spawn and query other agents' blocked/idle state without babysitting terminals.
